root_cause.text: The driver relied on hardware automatic chip select control for the built-in CS, which unconditionally asserted the CS whenever data was written to the transmit buffer, causing bus conflicts when multiple devices (one using built-in CS, others using GPIO CS) were attached.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "the in-built chip select is set low while linux tries to access the device attached to the GPIO." The patch adds software control of the built-in CS via `DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL` and implements a `set_cs` callback, and removes the previous `mchp_coreqspi_setup_op` that did not disable automatic CS control. The commit message explicitly says "Modify the driver so that it controls chip select directly" because automatic control caused the CS to be low for active-high devices or during GPIO device access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement sets the control register bits to enable the controller without explicitly clearing the automatic chip select control bit, leaving hardware auto-CS active, which will assert the built-in CS whenever data is written to the transmit buffer, causing bus conflicts with GPIO CS devices.

This writes the control register value that includes the auto-CS behavior, committing the hardware configuration that causes the built-in CS to be asserted automatically on data writes, leading to conflicts with other devices using GPIO CS.

This assigns the transfer_one callback which writes data to the transmit buffer during transfers, thereby activating the hardware's automatic CS assertion and causing bus conflicts if other devices (using GPIO CS) are present on the same bus.

This sets the number of hardware chip selects to 2, but since the driver does not disable the hardware automatic CS (built-in CS0), the built-in CS will still assert during transfers even when a GPIO CS is used for another device, leading to bus conflicts.

This indicates that GPIO chip select descriptors are used for some devices, but the driver does not disable the hardware automatic chip select for the built-in CS, so the built-in CS still asserts during transfers, causing conflicts with the GPIO-controlled devices.

This function call configures the SPI operation but does not disable the automatic chip select control, so subsequent data writes during the operation still trigger unwanted built-in CS assertion, contributing to bus conflicts when multiple devices are attached.

bic_trace_step.reason: The driver in this initial commit does not manage chip select (CS) explicitly. It relies entirely on the hardware's automatic CS assertion when data is written to the transmit buffer (e.g., in mchp_coreqspi_write_op and mchp_coreqspi_read_op).
